account:
Today appears quiet and orderly rather than unusual. I read my appointment book this morning, visited the market, reviewed accounts with the secretary, took tea with my neighbour at the east-dock cottage, and returned for the builder's 16:30 office appointment. The treasury held 128 emeralds when checked; the secretary reported no outstanding bills or confirmed delivery assignments. The baker reported a well-stocked stall and eight emeralds in sales. My neighbour has noticed nothing needing attention around the cottages.

Freight has been asking about deliveries and offering ferry crossings. As far as I know, this is an effort to find transport work; I have authorized no deliveries. The builder's appointment was described as a repair review, but he reports no confirmed defects at the bridge, landing, or warehouse and recommends against unnecessary repairs. He is asking what work I want done this week. I have requested a proposed maintenance-inspection scope and fee, and have authorized no spending. This looks like routine maintenance planning, not evidence of a particular problem. The secretary is present and says written office notes are secured beside my appointment book. I should clarify whether any further inspection is actually needed before commissioning anything. My next scheduled destination is home at 19:00; tomorrow's appointments include a 10:00 grain inspection at the mill.
